title: Vinod Kumar v. State of U.P.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Dilip Gupta, J.; Jayant Banerji, J.
disposition: Writ dismissed; petitioner relegated to Clause 6.5.
headnote: A writ challenging a demand notice to deposit Rs. 5,26,560 was dismissed because the consumer, who disputed the amount, had an alternative remedy under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.
facts: Vinod Kumar filed a writ petition in the Allahabad High Court challenging a notice dated 1 March 2017 asking him to deposit Rs. 5,26,560. He disputed that amount. Counsel for Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited submitted that the petitioner had an alternative remedy under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The Court accepted that submission and dismissed the petition on the alternative remedy.

holding_units.holding: A consumer who disputes the amount demanded in a notice to deposit has an alternative remedy under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and a writ petition challenging that notice is dismissed on that ground.

not_decided.point: Correctness of the demand of Rs. 5,26,560 in the notice dated 1 March 2017
